title: BSU vs PSU: tuition, size, location
summary: Boise State University (BSU) versus Portland State University (PSU). Also searched as PSU vs BSU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Boise State University (BSU) and Portland State University (PSU) are both public institutions, but they differ in several key aspects. BSU, located in Boise, has a larger undergraduate enrollment of 17,674 students compared to PSU's 13,182 students in Portland. Additionally, the in-state tuition at BSU is $9,048, which is lower than PSU's in-state tuition of $11,679. These differences reflect variations in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance between Boise State University (BSU) and Portland State University (PSU), BSU offers a lower in-state tuition rate of $9,048 compared to PSU's $11,679. For out-of-state students, BSU's tuition is $27,788, while PSU's is higher at $31,074. Despite these differences in tuition fees, the median debt for students who complete their degrees is the same at both institutions, amounting to $20,500. These figures highlight the financial considerations prospective students might evaluate when choosing between BSU and PSU.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Boise State University (BSU) and Portland State University (PSU) both offer traditional campus-based learning models in urban settings. BSU is situated in Boise, Idaho, while PSU is located in Portland, Oregon. The undergraduate enrollment at BSU is larger, with 17,674 students compared to PSU's 13,182. Both universities provide a range of academic programs and campus facilities that support in-person learning experiences, reflecting their roles as public institutions serving their respective metropolitan areas.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Boise State University (BSU) and Portland State University (PSU) are both accredited public institutions, ensuring that they meet established standards of quality in higher education. Accreditation supports the recognition of their academic programs and facilitates the transfer of credits. While specific accrediting bodies are not detailed here, both universities maintain accreditation status that aligns with their roles as comprehensive universities serving their respective regions.

sections.heading: Pick BSU if
paragraphs: When deciding between Boise State University (BSU) and Portland State University (PSU), prospective students might pick BSU if they prefer a public institution with a higher admission rate, as BSU admits approximately 87.21% of applicants. BSU also offers a more affordable in-state tuition of $9,048 compared to PSU. Additionally, BSU has a completion rate of 60.2% within 150% of the expected time, which may appeal to students seeking a supportive environment for degree completion. These factors make BSU a suitable choice for those prioritizing accessibility, cost, and timely graduation.

sections.heading: Pick PSU if
paragraphs: Pick Portland State University (PSU) if you are looking for a public institution with a high admission rate, as PSU admits approximately 90.87% of applicants. Although PSU's in-state tuition of $11,679 is higher than Boise State University's, it may be a suitable option for students prioritizing accessibility. PSU has a completion rate of 52.66% within 150% of the expected time, reflecting its commitment to supporting students through degree completion. These factors make PSU a viable choice for those seeking an open admission policy and a public university environment.
